CORRECTIONS APPLIED to this entry's original text: (1) the remote client is an SPA, NOT iOS -- the iOS wording is stale; SPA framework choice is deliberately OUT OF SCOPE; (2) the agent boundary is the OFFICIAL GitHub Copilot SDK for Go (github.com/github/copilot-sdk/go, pinned v1.0.11 = commit a550258d5c37bd662197536992a23d633bfe5804), NOT coder/acp-go-sdk -- intercom-go implements no ACP broker, no ACP wire protocol, and no direct headless-Copilot-CLI lifecycle. That the SDK internally manages a Copilot CLI server over JSON-RPC is an SDK IMPLEMENTATION DETAIL (its codec is under internal/ and unimportable by hosts); (3) the three load-bearing conflicts recorded here are RESOLVED: durability -- the backend projection is a CACHE and the SDK runtime is the durable event source via GetEvents/ResumeSession, bridged by the D4a minimal session pointer (a pointer, not a store; D7 full persistence remains deferred); operator surface in the persistence schema -- moot, Slack is retired so slack_ts/thread_ts/channel_id vanish with it; lifecycle ownership -- settled as one isolated process per workspace, orchestrated by autoharness, one allocated HTTP/WS port (the second ACP port is gone). Follow-up: internal/pathsafe hardening opportunities identified during 015-S adversarial review (advisory-only, no P0/P1, not required for 015-S merge): (1) addLongPathPrefix's \\.\ device-namespace exclusion branch is currently unreachable given filepath.IsAbs's own device-path handling -- add a locking assertion or restructure so the branch's reachability is independently verified. (2) MAX_PATH threshold (260) and length-comparison use UTF-8 byte length as a proxy for the UTF-16 code-unit count Windows actually measures -- safe/conservative direction but imprecise for non-ASCII paths; consider a rune-aware or UTF-16-aware comparison. (3) getFinalPathNameByHandle allocates a fresh buffer per call; consider pooling if Resolve call volume grows materially beyond the documented 10-100-paths-per-root case. (4) The GOOS=windows lint CI step duplicates full-repo lint runtime; consider scoping it to windows-tagged packages only if CI time becomes a concern. Source: 015-S multi-persona adversarial review round (Go/Correctness/Concurrency/Maintainability/Architecture reviewers), all P2/P3, zero P0/P1. === STAGE DISPOSITION 2026-09-10 (dark-factory cycle, shipment 016-S QUEUED) : PARTIALLY HARVESTED -- REMAINS ACTIVE, NOT ARCHIVED. Items (1) and (2) were harvested into feature 017-F / queued shipment 016-S; items (3) and (4) are DEFERRED and are the reason this entry is retained rather than archived. ITEM (1) -> 017.002-T, WITH A MATERIAL PREMISE CORRECTION: this entry asserted addLongPathPrefix's \\.\ device-namespace branch is 'currently unreachable given filepath.IsAbs's own device-path handling'. THAT PREMISE IS FALSE. Measured this cycle with an isolated go run probe: filepath.IsAbs returns TRUE for \\.\C:\foo (VolumeName \\.\C:), \\.\PhysicalDrive0, \\.\UNC\srv\sh\x, and for a 307-character \\.\-prefixed path. The !filepath.IsAbs early return does NOT shadow the branch -- THE BRANCH IS REACHABLE. What is actually true is narrower: within the guard order (\\?\ -> \\.\ -> \\) the branch is REACHABLE BUT BEHAVIOURALLY REDUNDANT, because the immediately-following generic \\ guard returns the identical value for any \\.\ input. Independently confirmed by the Correctness Reviewer during adversarial plan review. 017.002-T therefore keeps the branch (deletion rejected: removes self-documenting intent and couples correctness to the adjacent guard's continued existence), locks its observable verdict with an order-independent characterization test, and corrects the stale prose. A panic/unreachability assertion was REJECTED BY NAME -- the premise is false, and docs/compound/build-errors/go-race-requires-cgo-fails-closed-2026-09-03.md records a prior incident of exactly this failure mode (defensive scaffolding on an unverified premise becoming review-finding surface for no safety benefit). ITEM (2) -> 017.003-T: MAX_PATH threshold made UTF-16-code-unit-aware. Measured: 200 x U+00E9 = 400 UTF-8 bytes / 200 UTF-16 units; 100 x U+1F600 = 400 bytes / 200 units. UTF-8 byte length is ALWAYS >= UTF-16 code-unit count (1->1, 2->1, 3->1, 4->2), so the existing proxy fires at or before the true limit -- it can only produce a FALSE POSITIVE, never a false negative. CONFIRMED: this is a PRECISION improvement, NOT a correctness or security defect, and framing it as a vulnerability fix is an explicit anti-goal. A rune count was rejected (a surrogate pair is 1 rune but 2 UTF-16 code units, which would introduce the false negative the current code never has). The deliberation's original 'non-allocating bespoke counter' option was WITHDRAWN at plan review as gold-plating; 017.003-T uses utf16.Encode or a plain range accumulator. Plan review additionally surfaced and ACCEPTED decision D-10: dropping the \\?\ prefix in the precision-gain band re-enables ordinary Win32 normalization (trailing dot/space stripping, reserved device names CON/NUL/AUX) for those paths, which is exactly how every sub-MAX_PATH path already behaves today. ITEMS (3) AND (4) DEFERRED -- WHY THIS ENTRY IS NOT ARCHIVED: item (3) getFinalPathNameByHandle buffer pooling and item (4) scoping the GOOS=windows lint CI step are BOTH pure performance / CI-runtime optimizations with ZERO correctness or security content, and the operator's scope note for this cycle named ONLY 'device namespace branch reachability and UTF-16-aware MAX_PATH handling'. Under the operator prioritization framework (simplicity supersedes complexity; reliability and security supersede feature work) and YAGNI, implementing them now would be scope expansion against a documented 10-100-paths-per-root call volume that has not grown. Independently adjudicated CORRECT by the Scope Boundary Auditor during plan review (zero P0/P1 on scope). This entry remains the ONLY tracker for items (3) and (4). Archive when those two are either implemented or explicitly retired. MATERIAL CORRECTION MADE THIS CYCLE (adversarial review, Scope Boundary Auditor P2), recorded rather than silently dropped: an earlier Stage draft argued call volume is ZERO because Root.Resolve has zero callers. THAT REASONING WAS WRONG. getFinalPathNameByHandle is reached by a second, independent path that does not involve Resolve at all: config.Validate (internal/config/validate.go:42 and :67) -> pathsafe.NewRoot -> canonicalizeReparse (internal/pathsafe/root.go:346) -> getFinalPathNameByHandle. The ACCURATE measurement is: Root.Resolve specifically has ZERO production callers, but getFinalPathNameByHandle IS reachable in the non-test call graph at a volume of ONE CALL PER NewRoot -- one for DefaultWorkspaceRoot plus one per configured mapping, evaluated once at config-validation time. That is a handful of calls per process start, FAR BELOW the documented 10-100-paths-per-root case and nowhere near 'materially beyond' it; additionally no wired entrypoint reaches config validation today (both cmd/intercom and cmd/intercom-ctl return errNotImplemented). Trigger has NOT fired -- but now on correct grounds (volume far below threshold) rather than false grounds (zero reachability). Independently assessed by the Architecture Strategist: a 520-byte MAX_PATH pool cannot dominate two syscalls plus two encodings, the grow path allocates anyway, and pooling would add buffer-lifetime rules (do not Put a grown slice; do not retain after UTF16ToString) to a NON-NEGOTIABLE control for no measured win. ITEM (4) scoping the GOOS=windows golangci-lint CI step -- trigger is 'if CI TIME BECOMES A CONCERN'. MEASURED THIS CYCLE against real code-bearing CI runs: total wall clock 155s / 150s / 139s (runs 34557397128, 34556894501, 34556094063), i.e. about 2.5 minutes. Per-job breakdown of run 34557397128: test (windows, advisory) 104s, lint 102s, test 101s, security 52s, ci gate 39s. TWO DECISIVE FINDINGS: (a) CI time is not a concern; (b) the lint job is NOT EVEN ON THE CRITICAL PATH -- lint, expensive/test and windows all share `needs: changes` with no inter-dependency and run CONCURRENTLY, and test (windows, advisory) at 104s is LONGER than lint at 102s, so shaving the second golangci-lint invocation would move total CI time by approximately ZERO. Most of the lint job is `go install golangci-lint@v2.13.2` (compiling the linter); the GOOS=windows re-run reuses that binary and a warm build cache, so its MARGINAL cost is a fraction of the 102s. ADDITIONALLY THE PROPOSED CHANGE IS COVERAGE-NEGATIVE: the step exists precisely because (per its own 016.001-T comment) 'the repository's only lint gate is GOOS-scoped via Go file discovery, so the //go:build windows-tagged production surface under internal/pathsafe ... was never analyzed'. Narrowing it to windows-tagged packages only would stop analyzing GOOS-conditional behaviour in every OTHER package under the Windows tag set -- reducing BLOCKING static-analysis coverage over a NON-NEGOTIABLE Constitution III control to save ~0s of wall clock, which inverts the operator's own priority ordering (reliability/security supersede feature work). Note the asymmetry: the GOOS=windows lint step is BLOCKING while the Windows runtime test job is ADVISORY (continue-on-error unless WINDOWS_GATE_REQUIRED is set), so this step is the stronger of the two Windows gates and is the wrong one to weaken. Priority: low (provisional; performance-only, no correctness/security impact, explicitly matches an already-rejected plan option).=== STAGE DISPOSITION 2026-09-11 (dark-factory cycle, P-017; chartered scope BF5DE670/6B751D8B/475E76D2): ACCEPT-AS-IS (do nothing, matching plan precedent) -- REMAINS ACTIVE, NOT ARCHIVED, CONTRIBUTES NO TASK. SOUNDNESS IS NOT THE ISSUE: the proposed byte-length fast-path guard is mathematically SOUND -- len(path) >= utf16Len(path) holds for ASCII, 2-, 3-, and 4-byte UTF-8 sequences and for invalid UTF-8 (replacement rune), so len(path) < 260 implies utf16Len(path) < 260 with NO possibility of a false negative. This was independently re-proved by the Correctness Reviewer during this cycle's adversarial decision review. The guard is deferred ON VALUE, NEVER ON SAFETY. WHY DEFERRED: (a) utf16Len is ALREADY allocation-free (a plain `for _, r := range path` accumulator -- no []rune, no []uint16), so the guard would skip a bounded loop, not a decode; (b) the immediate caller canonicalizeReparse then performs a lazy-DLL Find, a syscall.UTF16PtrFromString ALLOCATION, a syscall.CreateFile syscall, and a GetFinalPathNameByHandleW syscall, which dominate a <=260-iteration loop entirely; (c) no wired entrypoint reaches this path today -- both cmd/intercom and cmd/intercom-ctl return errNotImplemented. MATERIAL CORRECTION MADE THIS CYCLE (adversarial review, Scope Boundary Auditor P2): an earlier Stage draft asserted this code path "never executes in production" because Root.Resolve has zero callers. THAT ASSERTION WAS FALSE and is corrected here rather than silently dropped -- addLongPathPrefix IS reachable in the non-test call graph via config.Validate -> pathsafe.NewRoot -> canonicalizeReparse -> addLongPathPrefix (internal/config/validate.go:42 and :67; internal/pathsafe/root.go:346), entirely independent of Root.Resolve. The deferral conclusion is unchanged but now rests on correct grounds.
